query: Consider the following context: How to rationally design composition of alloys with desired properties has always been an open and challenging question, especially for high-entropy alloy (HEA) which has huge selections of composition due to the feature of multi-principal elements. Although great efforts have been made in the past decades, such as approaches based on thermo-kinetic analysis and simulations, strategies to quick determine the optimal HEA composition remain lacking. In that context, which method can be used for design intrinsically strong, ductile, and low-weight refractory HEA (RHEA) compositions, and why?

generation.hypothesis: A computational framework integrating machine learning and density functional theory can be used to design intrinsically strong, ductile, and low-weight refractory high-entropy alloy (RHEA) compositions by predicting the properties of HEAs and RHEAs.
generation.material_initial_state: Multi-principal elements with huge selections of composition
generation.intervention: Developing a computational framework that integrates machine learning and density functional theory
generation.conditions: General operating conditions for HEAs and RHEAs
generation.mechanism: Machine learning algorithms predict the properties of HEAs and RHEAs based on their composition and crystal structure, while density functional theory provides accurate calculations of the electronic structure and thermodynamic properties
generation.predicted_outcome: A 20% increase in strength, 30% increase in ductility, and 15% reduction in weight compared to existing RHEA compositions
generation.boundary: The computational framework is limited to predicting properties of HEAs and RHEAs with up to 5 principal elements
generation.uncertainty: The accuracy of the computational framework may be affected by the quality of the training data and the complexity of the machine learning algorithms

falsification_experiment.design: A computational simulation study using the developed framework to predict the properties of a set of RHEA compositions, followed by experimental validation of the predicted properties
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the predicted properties deviate by more than 10% from the experimentally measured values for at least 80% of the tested compositions, the hypothesis is falsified
